summary: Iteration 7 retest after MapCanvas isDragging fix. FRONTEND UNBLOCKED: galaxy renders (28 circles, 26 groups), no runtime overlay, ResourceHUD shows T:3 M:3 C:3, EspionagePanel + all 4 buttons visible & enabled (tech=3), TurnRecap modal opens on Resolve Turn. Also found & fixed a SECONDARY blocker: App.js scheduleEspionage/cancelEspionage referenced `axios` which is NOT imported (App.js uses fetch elsewhere) — ReferenceError on click, POST never fired. Replaced with fetch(). After fix, POST /api/game/{id}/espionage-orders fires with correct body {player_id, orders:[{kind:'destabilize', systemId:...}]}. Backend returns 400 (kernel rejects self-targeted destabilize — expected kernel-level validation, not a wiring bug). Backend regression: 39/40 pytest pass. Only failure is the known kernel-side gap `snapshot.players` missing (documented in iter 6, explicitly out-of-scope per main agent instructions). New /recap unknown-viewer 404 validation works (test_03 passes).

minor.issue: recap.snapshot missing `players` key. Kernel host.ts::recapFor exposes {turn, phase, systems, resources, combat} but not `players`. DOCUMENTED KERNEL-SIDE GAP owned by Grok — do NOT fix backend-side.

Returns 400 when destabilize target is the acting player's own system. Likely correct kernel validation but no error body returned to help the UI display a reason. Consider surfacing kernel reason string.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED. Called `axios.post` but axios is not imported anywhere in App.js (rest of file uses fetch). ReferenceError swallowed by try/catch, so no POST was ever sent when a user clicked any EspionagePanel button. Rewrote both handlers to use fetch() with JSON body + status check.

issues: Owner text appears twice in system info (line 4 and line 10). Minor duplication in OrdersTray/info-panel composition.

rca_of_the_issue: Two bugs found this iteration. (1) MapCanvas.jsx isDragging prop — FIXED by main agent before retest (App.js:2809 now passes isDragging={isDragging}, MapCanvas.jsx:16 destructures it). (2) NEW: App.js:997 & 1013 called `axios.post` but axios was never imported (only fetch is used elsewhere). Chrome reported `ReferenceError: axios is not defined` which the try/catch swallowed as a warning; UI updated local queue optimistically but no request ever hit the backend. Repro: select any system -> click Sabotage/Destabilize/Counter -> observe console warning, no network request. Mitigation applied: replaced both axios calls with fetch(), added !r.ok error propagation to preserve rollback semantics. Post-fix: POST body verified {"player_id":"p-...","orders":[{"kind":"destabilize","system_id":"sys-...",...}]} — backend receives + kernel processes (returns 400 when target is self, expected).
